The '''PTB-625 planetary bomber''' was a [[Bomber/Legends|bomber]] that was jointly produced by the [[Incom Corporation/Legends|Incom Corporation]] and [[Sublight Products Corporation]].<ref name="ROTS:ICS" /> With a narrow spaceframe flanked by large [[Engine/Legends|engines]], the PTB-625 resembled other Incom/Subpro [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] such as the [[Z-95 Headhunter/Legends|Z-95 Headhunter]], [[NTB-630 naval bomber/Legends|NTB-630 naval bomber]], and the [[Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 starfighter/Legends|ARC-170]].<ref name="DB">{{DB|starship|arc170fighter|ARC-170 starfighter}}</ref> The PTB-625 was not as maneuverable as the NTB-630 and was designed for [[Planet/Legends|planetary]] bombardment.<ref name="CSWE" /> It was in common use by [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Republic Navy/Legends|Navy]] forces in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]<ref name="ROTS:ICS" /> of [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].<ref name="The New Essential Chronology">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The PTB-625 bomber was first mentioned in the [[2005]] ''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith Incredible Cross-Sections]]'', a book detailing vehicles seen in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]. Later, the page mentioning the PTB-625 was reprinted in ''[[Star Wars: Complete Cross-Sections]]'', and the bomber received a mention in the [[Databank (original)|Databank]] entry of the ARC-170 starfighter on [[StarWars.com]], as well as in ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' entry of the NTB-630 bomber. The PTB-625 was later mentioned in [[2012]]'s ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'', by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Paul R. Urquhart]]. It was eventually pictured in The ''Star Wars: Age of Rebellion'' Rules Supplement [[Stay on Target (sourcebook)|''Stay on Target'']].

The written profile of the PTB-625 in ''Stay on Target'' is completely at odds with the illustration used for said profile, explicitly calling the vehicle a “design departure from other Incom/SubPro products” and describing it as a massive flying wing driven by six ion turbofan thrusters, armed with twin light laser cannons mounted in a forward turret and fixed mountings on the dorsal and ventral fuselage each containing twin autoblasters. There has been no official explanation for the discrepancy as of this writing.
